It is located in {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}}.

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} of {{ill|Soejimo district|ja|添下郡|zh|添下郡|qid=Q11560415}}, and is thought to form a paired shrine with {{ill|Sugata Shrine (Yamatokōriyama)|ja|菅田神社 (大和郡山市)|qid=Q134888232|lt=Sugata Shrine}}.

Under the system of {{ill|Emperor Daigo|ar|الإمبراطور دايغو|arz|امبيرور دايجو|azb|دایقو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Daigo|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر دایگۆ|cs|Daigo|de|Daigo|el|Αυτοκράτορας Νταϊγκό|eo|Daigo (imperiestro)|es|Daigo Tennō|fa|امپراتور دایگو|fr|Daigo|id|Kaisar Daigo|it|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|ko|다이고 천황|ms|Maharaja Daigo|nl|Daigo (keizer)|pl|Daigo|pt|Daigo|ru|Император Дайго|sh|Car Daigo|sl|Cesar Daigo|sv|Daigo (kejsare)|sw|Daigo wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิไดโงะ|tl|Emperador Daigo|tr|Daigo (imparator)|uk|Імператор Дайґо|ur|شہنشاہ ڈائیگو|vi|Thiên hoàng Daigo|yo|Emperor Daigo|zh|醍醐天皇|zh_min_nan|Daigo Thian-hông|zh_yue|醍醐天皇|qid=Q329753}} and the Engi regulations, it received offerings of hoes and quivers in the {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|simple|Kinensai|th|คิเน็นไซ|qid=Q118906710}}<ref>From Shinto ritual materials.</ref>.

It was formerly called “Shinoda-sha (Shinoda-no-miya)” and is said to have stood at Kita-Shinoda, about 500 m north of the current site, on the east side of Tsutsui Elementary School.

== Overview ==
In conclusion, the enshrined deity is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Izunome-no-Kami}}<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://meta01.library.pref.nara.jp/opac/repository/repo/65/?lang=0&mode=0&opkey=R166362381017073&idx=41 |title=Soekami District Shrine Register, p.108 |access-date=2024-4-26}}</ref>. However, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmeichō}}, it is written as “Sugatahime Shrine, two seats”<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1273537/1/44 |title=Engishiki Jinmeichō |access-date=2024-4-26}}</ref>. Also, in {{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092}} and in Shinto source materials, the deities are listed as Sugatahime-no-Kami and {{ill|Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Mikoto|ja|天目一箇神|ko|아메노마히토쓰노카미|zh|天目一箇神|qid=Q10016750|lt=Amekushimahitotsu-no-Mikoto}}<ref>The same deities are listed in ''Study of Shikinaisha, Vol. 2''.</ref>, and in ''Yamato-shi'' as well, Izunome-no-Kami is treated as doubtful. Izunome-no-Kami is the deity born when Izanagi returned from Yomi and performed purification, with “Izu” meaning sacred purification. However, from the shrine name itself, it is clear that Sugatahime-no-Kami was worshiped.

== Precinct shrines ==
*Hachiman Shrine (deity: Homuda-wake-no-Mikoto)
*Kasuga Shrine (Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto)
*Kōra Shrine (Takeuchi no Sukune)
*Kamo Shrine (Kotoshironushi-no-Kami)
*Inari Shrine (Inari Daimyōjin)
*Jibutsudō Hall (seated Yakushi Nyorai image)<ref>''History of Kōriyama Town''</ref>
